messages:
eli: FYI customer AcmeGames filed a P99 complaint — reported p99 ~5.8s for /v1/generate from their Dedicated pool around 2026-02-15 12:05 UTC. They attached trace ids and a curl.
support-bot: alert: high p99 /v1/generate for cust=AcmeGames pool=d-ed-42, p95 1.2s -> p99 5.8s, attach queue depth spike at 12:03 UTC. link: https://dash.redwood/acme/pools/d-ed-42
maria: looking at provisioning metrics — attach backlog jumps ~12:02, attach success rate drops, autoscaler started scaleup but new nodes took ~90s to attach. cold_gpu_start metric shows multiple cold starts at once.
nisha: can you paste a sample of the client's request shape? heavy seq len?
eli: they sent many small chat requests, seq len ~64, but QPS bursty (200 RPS sustained for ~30s). Their pool has reserved=8 gpus, autoscale max=32.
ben: autoscaler logs: 
```
2026-02-15T12:02:01Z INFO scale-request pool=d-ed-42 desired=24 current=8 pending=16
2026-02-15T12:02:15Z WARN attach-backoff throttle=200ms reason=attach-concurrency
2026-02-15T12:03:10Z ERROR attach-failed instance=i-0a12 msg=timeout waiting for image
```

maria: attach concurrency limit kicked in because fairshare counts were low for this pool (we've got other pools competing). Also image pulling delays on the AZ.
eli: customer says they saw 429s initially then 200s that took long. Support reproduced a p99 spike with their payload. Repro steps they used: 
```
for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"gpt-neo-8k","input":"hi","max_tokens":64}'; done
```

nisha: ok. Immediate mitigations: 1) move them to a pre-warmed capacity (dedicated reserved) temporary, or 2) lower their route concurrency (rate-limit / retry with linear backoff) and enable fallback to a smaller model variant. Which is feasible quickly?
ben: ops-bot can bump fairshare for pool d-ed-42 in the scheduler for 15m to prioritize attach tokens. Command: `ops-bot bump-fairshare d-ed-42 --duration 15m --reason "customer p99 escalation"`
ops-bot: executed bump-fairshare d-ed-42 duration=15m new-weight=8 by=ben
maria: also reimage/cache issue: registry responded slowly in that AZ; we can instruct autoscaler to prefer another AZ for next attaches. I'll open provisioning ticket to reduce image pull time.
eli: actionable list for support thread: 
- Temporarily bump fairshare (done).
- Move customer to pre-warm (support can open a reserved request).
- Apply a short rate-limit on their endpoint and suggest exponential retry client-side.
- Add image cache warmup for pool nodes in that AZ.
- Postmortem to examine autoscaler backoff parameters and cold-gpu start latency.

nisha: reproduction note: when we spam attach requests locally with `./tooling/attach-stress --pool d-ed-42 --concurrency 50` we hit the attach-backoff path reliably and p99 jumps. I'll add that as a unit repro in the ticket.

ben: temporary customer communication: "We're prioritizing your pool to reduce p99, and provisioning additional capacity now. Recommend short retries (500–1000ms) if you see 429s for next 15 minutes." @support please send.

eli: support message sent. Customer asked for ETA — estimate 10-15m to see improvement after fairshare bump and subsequent attachments finishing.

maria: long-term followups: 
- tune autoscaler attach concurrency/backoff heuristics to avoid thundering attach when desired delta is large,
- implement staggered node boot to avoid many cold starts simultaneously,
- expand node image cache replication to other AZs,
- consider aggressive pre-warm thresholds based on burst detection for high QPS customers.

nisha: filing incident ticket P-10234 with logs, repro, and dashboards. tagging eng-sre and eng-platform.

ben: thanks all. I'll monitor dashboards for p99. If no improvement in 15m we escalate to oncall.

ops-bot: monitor: p99 /v1/generate cust=AcmeGames now 3.9s -> decreasing after bump. will report again in 10m.

eli: closing here when ops-bot confirms stable p99 < 1.5s.
